## Comparative Biochemistry and Physiology Part D: Genomics and Proteomics

Volume 59, September 2026, 101858

# Histological and transcriptomic analysis of the white hepatopancreas in Amphioctopus fangsiao

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cbd.2026.101858Get rights and content

## Highlights

  * •

The white and normal hepatopancreas of Amphioctopus fangsiao were compared in this study.

  * •

The white hepatopancreas showed distinct structural features.

  * •

A total of 3257 differentially expressed genes were identified between two tissues.

  * •

Fifteen genes have been identified as being beneficial for the production of ink.

  * •

The white hepatopancreas plays a key role in ink production and defense in octopus.

## Abstract

Ink production and release is one of the most important defense strategies in cephalopods. Previous studies have shown that ink production and release are closely associated with the hepatopancreas. In octopuses, the ink sac is embedded within the hepatopancreas, and the surrounding hepatopancreatic tissue appears white. To explore the differences between the white hepatopancreas and normal hepatopancreas, as well as the potential function of the white hepatopancreas, this study took Amphioctopus fangsiao as the research object and conducted histological and transcriptomic studies on white hepatopancreas and normal hepatopancreas tissues. Histological analysis revealed clear structural differences between the two tissues, with lipid droplets absent in the white hepatopancreas. Transcriptomic analysis identified 6530 differentially expressed genes (DEGs). Gene Ontology (GO), Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG), and protein–protein interaction (PPI) analyses found that oxidative phosphorylation and the Apelin signaling pathways were significantly enriched in white hepatopancreas, suggesting an increase in ATP production and the alleviation of oxidative stress. Members of the ABHD gene family enriched may regulate lipid droplet metabolism. TAT, SLC6A6, Dop1R1 and Dop2R could potentially influence the levels of tyrosine, taurine and dopamine in the white hepatopancreas. Considering that these substances are involved in the main components of ink, we speculate that these genes may be related to the precursor supply for ink production. Our study demonstrates that the white hepatopancreas is structurally distinct from the normal hepatopancreas, and may be functionally related to the ink sac to some extent.

## Introduction

Coleoid cephalopods, mainly including Octopoda (octopuses) and Decapoda (squids and cuttlefish), occupy important positions in marine ecosystems and have great economic values (Boavida-Portugal et al., 2022). Amphioctopus fangsiao, belonging to the order Octopoda, is widely distributed in China, Japan, and South Korea, and has become an important traditional coastal food in these regions (Wang et al., 2015). Owing to its strong tolerance to captive conditions, efficient feed utilization, high reproductive capacity, and fast growth performance, this species shows considerable potential for aquaculture production and stock enhancement programs (Garcia de la serrana et al., 2020).

Ink ejection is a defense mechanism unique to coleoid cephalopods and is typically categorized into two types “smoke screens” and “pseudomorphs” (Bush and Robison, 2007). The primary function of the smoke screen is to create visual interference that obscures the predator's view. The pseudomorph acts as a decoy, potentially distracting the predator and increasing the chance of escape (Bush and Robison, 2007). In addition, ink also functions as an intraspecific communication medium, releasing specific chemical signals that can induce conspecific individuals to initiate inking behavior or shift their defensive state (Wood et al., 2008). The melanin-rich component of ink is produced by the ink gland within the ink sac in cephalopods. During the defense process, the secretion in the ink sac lumen is released via a duct into the mantle cavity, and is then expelled through the funnel opening while mixing with the secretion from the funnel (Derby, 2014). Studies have shown that ink production and release is an energy-intensive process involving the coordinated action of multiple metabolic pathways and complex biochemical reactions (Palumbo, 2003).

As the central metabolic regulatory organ in cephalopods, the hepatopancreas serves as the primary site for digestion, nutrient absorption, and energy storage. It also performs essential functions in detoxification and immune defense, and plays a key role in metabolic regulation in response to environmental stress (Vilarnau et al., 2024). The study in A. fangsiao have demonstrated that pathogenic bacteria or endotoxins originating from the intestinal microbiota are intercepted and detoxified by the hepatopancreas (Li et al., 2024). Excessive environmental microplastic exposure can cause toxic damage in A. fangsiao, and the hepatopancreas initiates detoxification responses to maintain physiological homeostasis (Zheng et al., 2022). Some researches have found that inking had significant effects on the histology, metabolome, immunity and physiological activity of the hepatopancreas. The activities of hexokinase (HK), pyruvate kinase (PK), superoxide dismutase (SOD) and malondialdehyde (MDA), as well as the expression of heat shock protein 90 (HSP90), heat shock protein 70 (HSP70), catalase (CAT), glutathione peroxidase (GPX) and arginine kinase (AK) in the hepatopancreas of cuttlefish Sepia pharaonis showed a rapid increase after the inking event (Jiang et al., 2019, Jiang et al., 2022). Inking stress also induced histopathological changes in the hepatopancreas of S. pharaonis. Metabolomic analyses further showed that inking stress initiated an acute metabolic response in the hepatopancreas, which caused the reduction of glucose, glycogen, adenosine triphosphate (ATP) and disturbed amino acid metabolism (Jiang et al., 2021). These demonstrate that the hepatopancreas plays a crucial role in defense response to inking stress.

The hepatopancreas of the octopuses in cephalopods are closely integrated with the ink sac. The ink sac is completely embedded within the parenchyma of the hepatopancreas. At the junction of the two organs, a previously unreported white heterogeneous tissue is observed (Fig. 1). This structure does not exist in squids and cuttlefish, where the ink sac is separate from the hepatopancreas (Boyle and Rodhouse, 2005). This pronounced structural difference may suggest that the white hepatopancreas tissue differs functionally from normal hepatopancreas of octopuses. To date, no studies have reported the physiological functions of this white hepatopancreatic tissue and the reason for the heterogeneity of the hepatopancreas.

In this study, we focused on A. fangsiao as the research subject and utilized histological methods to compare the structural characteristics of the hepatopancreas and the white hepatopancreas. Subsequently, transcriptomic analysis was conducted to screen for the differentially expressed genes in the white hepatopancreas relative to the normal hepatopancreas. Through GO and KEGG enrichment analyses and protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analysis, key genes in the white hepatopancreas were identified, and its potential biological functions were revealed. The expression patterns of the genes were further validated by quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR). This study reveals the gene expression characteristics and potential functional differences of the white hepatopancreas tissue for the first time, which will provide a theoretical basis for future studies aimed at distinguishing functional regions of the hepatopancreas and investigating the potential interaction between the ink sac and the hepatopancreas in A. fangsiao.

## Sample collection

In October 2023, 30 adult A. fangsiao individuals with an average body weight of 25.7 ± 3 g were collected from the Yellow Sea near Yantai and temporarily maintained in two glass tanks (length = 60 cm, width = 60 cm, height = 90 cm) for five days at 18 ± 0.5 °C. Air stones were placed in the tanks for aeration, and ceramic jars were provided as shelters to help the octopuses adapt to the rearing environment. Two kinds of tissues were collected, including hepatopancreas and white hepatopancreas.

The boundaries between them were clearly defined. The inner margin of each hepatic lobule was composed of a continuous layer of hepatocytes. ## Discussion

Ink production is a characteristic feature of Coleoid cephalopods (Derby, 2014). The hepatopancreas, as a major metabolic organ, plays an important role in the processes of ink production and release (Jiang et al., 2019). In this study, we investigated normal hepatopancreas and white hepatopancreas tissues. ## Conclusion

In this study, histological observations revealed clear structural differences between the hepatopancreas and the white hepatopancreas in A. fangsiao. Two key signaling pathways, the oxidative phosphorylation pathway and the Apelin signaling pathway, as well as the ABHD gene family and TAT, SLC6A6, Dop1R1, Dop2R genes were identified in white hepatopancreas through transcriptomic analysis. 11.5. Amphioctopus fangsiao (and other species of
Amphioctopus)
This is a small species with a mature ML typically around 50 mm and arms of subequal length except for arms 1,
which are conspicuously shorter; arms 4 are the longest by a small margin over arms 2 and 3. It is one of the easiest
octopuses to identify when alive or freshly dead because of the presence of a distinctive golden iridescent ring on the
outer surface of the interbrachial membrane between arms 2 and 3 of the right and left sides, and a broad pale -
coloured bar across the dorsal surface of the head (Figure 70; Sasaki, 1929; Gleadall and Naggs, 1991; Gleadall,
1997). The iridescent rings are components of each of a pair of ocelli (false eyespots), which the living octopus uses
to surprise and distract potential predators. After the octopus has died, however, the rings may appear only in rather
vague form (as shown on the octopus labelled 'O' in Figure 70), or may disappear altogether (as for the three animals
accompanying the specimen with the 'O' label; Figure 70). Similarly, the pale head bar can be obvious ('B' in Figure
70), or (after death) apparently absent (other animals in Figure 70). Several other species in this genus (including A.
aegina, A. ovulum, A. kagoshimensis and A. marginatus), both domestic and imported, and with or without ocelli, all
tend to be identified in Japanese markets using the vernacular name for A. fangsiao: 'iidako.'

Figure 70. Commercially packed Amphioctopus fangsiao imported from Hyogo Pref., obtained in Naha market,
Okinawa (image: C. Timmons). B, bar, broad and pale in colour, across the dorsal surface of the head, between the
eyes; O, gold-coloured iridescent ring component of an ocellus (false eyespot).

In this study, we describe the embryonic development of A. fangsiao from eggs to hatchlings, focusing on the formation of the mantle, eyes and arms. Results indicate that this species has several favorable characteristics for aquaculture, such as a short incubation period and a large body size of hatchlings. During the organogenesis, the primordia of organs, including the optic sac and arm crown, first appeared at stage VIII; then the mantle primordium, eye primordia and arm crown become visible at stage IX–X, and the rudiment of embryo (mantle, eyes and arms) was completely outlined at stage XI. The retinal pigment appeared yellowish at stage X–XI and gradually deepens in pigmentation in the subsequent stages, turning from yellowish to yellow, red, dark-red and eventually black. At stage XV, the primary lid fold, with only a circular opening remaining, covered the eye, and the dorsal ocular edge did not reach the ventral side until hatching (day 1–7). Afterwards, about 24 days after hatching, both the dorsal and ventral sides of eyelid could contract freely, with an oval and elongate slit remaining that was a miniature version of the adult morphology. The chromatophores and ink sac appeared at stage XIV. These observations provide a foundation for the reproductive biology and aquaculture of A. fangsiao and also offer an important reference for the research of embryonic development in related species.
